    "text": "The payload of a SUBSCRIBE Packet contains a list of Topic Filters\nindicating the Topics to which the Client wants to subscribe. The Topic\nFilters in a SUBSCRIBE packet payload MUST be UTF-8 encoded strings as\ndefined in Section 1.5.3 [MQTT-3.8.3-1] . A Server SHOULD support Topic\nfilters that contain the wildcard characters defined in Section 4.7.1 .\nIf it chooses not to support topic filters that contain wildcard\ncharacters it MUST reject any Subscription request whose filter contains\nthem [MQTT-3.8.3-2] . Each filter is followed by a byte called the\nRequested QoS. This gives the maximum QoS level at which the Server can\nsend Application Messages to the Client.\n\nThe payload of a SUBSCRIBE packet MUST contain at least one Topic Filter\n/ QoS pair. A SUBSCRIBE packet with no payload is a protocol violation\n[MQTT-3.8.3-3] . See section 4.8 for information about handling errors.\n\nThe requested maximum QoS field is encoded in the byte following each\nUTF-8 encoded topic name, and these Topic Filter / QoS pairs are packed\ncontiguously.\n\nFigure 3.22 – SUBSCRIBE Packet payload format\n\nDescription\n\n7\n\n6\n\n5\n\n4\n\n3\n\n2\n\n1\n\n0\n\nTopic Filter\n\nbyte 1\n\nLength MSB\n\nbyte 2\n\nLength LSB\n\nbytes 3..N\n\nTopic Filter\n\nRequested QoS\n\nReserved\n\nQoS\n\nbyte N+1\n\n0\n\n0\n\n0\n\n0\n\n0\n\n0\n\nX\n\nX\n\nThe upper 6 bits of the Requested QoS byte are not used in the current\nversion of the protocol. They are reserved for future use. The Server\nMUST treat a SUBSCRIBE packet as malformed and close the Network\nConnection if any of Reserved bits in the payload are non-zero, or QoS\nis not 0,1 or 2 [MQTT-3-8.3-4] .\n\n3.8.3.1 Payload non normative example\n\nFigure 3.23 - Payload byte format non normative example shows the\npayload for the SUBSCRIBE Packet briefly described in Table 3.5 -\nPayload non normative example ."

It MUST be a UTF-8 encoded string.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.2-2]\n\nThe Topic Name in the PUBLISH Packet MUST NOT contain wildcard\ncharacters.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.2-3]\n\nThe Topic Name in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Server to a subscribing\nClient MUST match the Subscription’s Topic Filter according to the\nmatching process defined in Section 4.7.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.4-1]\n\nThe receiver of a PUBLISH Packet MUST respond according to Table 3.4 -\nExpected Publish Packet response as determined by the QoS in the PUBLISH\nPacket.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.5-1]\n\nThe Server MUST deliver the message to the Client respecting the maximum\nQoS of all the matching subscriptions.\n\n[MQTT-3.3.5-2]\n\nIf a Server implementation does not authorize a PUBLISH to be performed\nby a Client; it has no way of informing that Client. It MUST either make\na positive acknowledgement, according to the normal QoS rules, or close\nthe Network Connection.\n\n[MQTT-3.6.1-1]\n\nBits 3,2,1 and 0 of the fixed header in the PUBREL Control Packet are\nreserved and MUST be set to 0,0,1 and 0 respectively. The Server MUST\ntreat any other value as malformed and close the Network Connection.\n\n[MQTT-3.8.1-1]\n\nBits 3,2,1 and 0 of the fixed header of the SUBSCRIBE Control Packet are\nreserved and MUST be set to 0,0,1 and 0 respectively. The Server MUST\ntreat any other value as malformed and close the Network Connection.\n\n[MQTT-3.8.3-1]\n\nThe Topic Filters in a SUBSCRIBE packet payload MUST be UTF-8 encoded\nstrings as defined in Section 1.5.3.\n\n[MQTT-3.8.3-2]\n\nIf the Server chooses not to support topic filters that contain wildcard\ncharacters it MUST reject any Subscription request whose filter contains\nthem.\n\n[MQTT-3.8.3-3]"

The Server might grant a\nlower maximum QoS than the subscriber requested. The QoS of Payload\nMessages sent in response to a Subscription MUST be the minimum of the\nQoS of the originally published message and the maximum QoS granted by\nthe Server. The server is permitted to send duplicate copies of a\nmessage to a subscriber in the case where the original message was\npublished with QoS 1 and the maximum QoS granted was QoS 0 [ MQTT-3\n.8.4-6] .\n\nNon normative examples If a subscribing Client has been granted maximum\nQoS 1 for a particular Topic Filter, then a QoS 0 Application Message\nmatching the filter is delivered to the Client at QoS 0. This means that\nat most one copy of the message is received by the Client.
